## Corrective Program Generator Engine — the 4-week program builder itself (2026-07-31)

Engine + data only, no coach UI, no member-facing surface (the next task builds the review/trigger UI), zero Your Move API calls (reads the already-classified local catalog only). Builds on the corrective metadata layer and MEF gap-fill exercises from the prior two tasks.

### Blueprints as data (`lib/corrective-engine/blueprints.ts`)

The 4 blueprints (Lower Cross, Upper Cross, Forward Head, Flat Back), each with tight-muscle slots (release/stretch/mobility candidates) and long-muscle slots (stability/strength candidates), exactly as recorded in `docs/CORRECTIVE_BLUEPRINT_GAP_CHECK.md`. This is now the single source of truth — `scripts/exercise-media/corrective-blueprint-gap-check.ts` (built in the prior task) was refactored to import from here instead of carrying its own duplicate copy of the same 4 blueprints, so the two can never drift apart. Verified byte-identical: re-ran the gap-check script after the refactor and diffed the regenerated `docs/CORRECTIVE_BLUEPRINT_GAP_CHECK.md` against git — zero changes.

### The MEF Method session template (`lib/corrective-engine/sessionBuilder.ts`)

Every session is full-body, 5 blocks in a fixed order — Release (role `release`, tight muscles only) → Mobility (role `stretch`/`mobility`, tight muscles only) → Stability (role `stability`/`strength`, long muscles, excluding TVA-type core-stability-only slots) → Strength (role `strength`, general full-body compound work, lower-body-led into upper body into a lower-strain accessory tail) → Core (role `core_stability` only, always last, prioritizing any active pattern's core-stability-only muscle like Lower Cross's TVA). Strength is omitted from the session entirely (not just left empty) whenever its budget is 0. A stacked program (e.g. Upper Cross + Forward Head, the task's own example) merges each blueprint's tight/long muscle slots, collapsing genuinely duplicate muscles (e.g. both blueprints' shared "upper traps" tight slot) into one, prioritized worst-severity-blueprint-first, with a defensive backstop that drops any muscle appearing as both tight and long across a stacked combination from both lists rather than risk a violation (not reachable with today's 4 blueprints, checked in case a 5th blueprint is added later without re-auditing this file).

**A real bug found and fixed by this engine's own guard test**: the first implementation matched a Release/Mobility candidate against a muscle slot correctly, but never checked whether that same exercise's *other* stretched muscles included one of the pattern's LONG muscles — e.g. a hamstring stretch that also happens to lengthen "lumbar erectors" (Flat Back's long muscle) was being selected for Flat Back's Mobility block because it correctly matched the "hamstrings" tight slot, silently violating "never stretch a pattern's long muscle" through the muscle it *wasn't* being selected for. Caught by the `never places a stretch/mobility pick against any active blueprint's LONG muscle` guard test failing on Flat Back (`expected [ 'lumbar erectors' ] to deeply equal []`) before this was ever reported as done. Fixed by adding an `excludeLabels` set (every active pattern's full long-muscle list) that every Release/Mobility candidate's entire `musclesStretched` array must clear, not just the one label that matched the slot.

### Severity dial (`lib/corrective-engine/blockBudgets.ts`)

Per-block exercise-count budgets, all inside the task's 8–12/session cap: mild 1/1/2/5/1 (release/mobility/stability/strength/core, 10 total, full strength block), moderate 2/2/3/3/1 (11 total, reduced strength), severe 3/3/4/0/2 (12 total, no Strength section at all — not just an empty one). Overall program severity is the worst individual detected pattern's severity, per the task.

### Posture-finding → blueprint mapping (`lib/corrective-engine/patternMapping.ts`, `findings.ts`) — a documented modeling decision

The Universal Registry's `PostureFindingType` vocabulary predates the 4 named blueprints, so only 2 of the 11 finding types map 1:1 (`forward_head`, `lower_crossed_pattern`). Upper Cross is inferred from `rounded_shoulders`/`elevated_shoulder`/`thoracic_kyphosis` (the real external signals a `static_posture` assessment produces for an upper-quadrant crossed pattern). Flat Back is inferred from `lumbar_posture`, which has no directional signal (it measures "outside neutral" without saying which way) — Lower Cross (hyperlordotic) and Flat Back (flattened) are opposite ends of the same lumbar-curvature spectrum, so `lumbar_posture` only produces a Flat Back pattern when `lower_crossed_pattern` is *not* also present on the same assessment, keeping the two mutually exclusive. A future dedicated finding type (or a directional lumbar signal) would make this a clean 1:1 mapping like the other two — noted here as a real follow-up, not treated as done. "Latest completed posture assessment" = `body_assessments` with `assessment_type: 'static_posture'` and `status` in `('analyzed', 'coach_reviewed')` (the two statuses this codebase's own action code only ever sets after findings actually exist); only `pending_review`/`confirmed`/`coach_overridden` findings count as real signal (dismissed/superseded/draft excluded).

### Exercise pool (`lib/corrective-engine/exercisePool.ts`)

Reads `mef_exercise_metadata` filtered to `spinal_flexion_core = false` and `equipment <@` the caller's allowed set (default `bodyweight`/`foam roller`/`ball`, matching the task's default assumption against the real equipment vocabulary this catalog actually uses), joined to `exercise_catalog` for display names in application code (no FK exists between the two tables — same precedent as `metadata.ts`/`normalize.ts`). **A real bug found before any test ran**: the first join fetched catalog names via `.in('external_id', [...825 ids])`, which blew past PostgREST's URL length limit (`URI too long`) once the exercise pool test actually ran against the real ~850-row catalog. Fixed by reading the whole (skinny, 2-column) catalog page-by-page via `range()` instead — the same "load the whole catalog for a comparison" precedent already used by `dedupe-exercise-catalog.ts` and the Your Move generation mapping.

### Seeded selection (`lib/corrective-engine/rng.ts`)

A small deterministic PRNG (FNV-1a string hash → mulberry32), no `Math.random()` anywhere — "rotate among qualified options via a seed, reproducible for the same seed" from a plain string seed. Candidates are always stably sorted by `externalId` before shuffling (DB query order isn't guaranteed stable across calls).

### Program generator + persistence (`programGenerator.ts`, `save.ts`)

One 4-week phase, `daysPerWeek` (2 or 3) distinct sessions, each independently seeded (`${seed}:session${i}`). The weekly session set repeats identically across all 4 weeks of this phase — a deliberate scope decision, not an oversight: phase-to-phase progression (mobility → stability → strength → power, power only from phase 2 on) is a separate concern this single-phase generator doesn't build, and this "one repeating week, the caller/reader replicates it" shape is the same convention already adopted elsewhere in this codebase for Your Move's own `/programs/generate` response. Output reuses the existing Coach Program Builder tables verbatim (`createTemplate`/`replaceTemplateContent`/`setTemplateStatus` from `lib/coach-program-builder/templates.ts`, zero new write path) — one `coach_program_templates` row per weekly session, all sharing a `program_tags` group id (`corrective-program:<uuid>`), same "a program is several templates, no new schema" precedent the Your Move program-generation feature already established. `corrective_tags` holds the detected blueprint keys; `coach_notes`/`description` record the detected patterns, severities, member, and seed for a coach's review. **Nothing is assigned** — `coach_program_assignments` is never touched, guard-tested directly (asserts a zero count).

### Schema (migration 131) — one additive change

`coach_program_templates.status` only ever had `draft`/`active`/`archived` (migration 82) — widened to add `pending_coach_review`, the same additive-constraint-widening convention already used repeatedly on this table's neighbors (`program_section`, `event_type`, etc.). Also widened `listCoachTemplates`'s default (no-filter) query from excluding just `archived` to excluding both `archived` and `pending_coach_review`, so an engine-generated draft stays invisible in the coach's existing Program Library browse view (`/coach/programs`) until a dedicated review screen exists (still reachable via an explicit `status: 'pending_coach_review'` filter) — a minimal necessary guard against an incomplete/confusing surface leaking into the current UI, not new UI work.

### CLI runner (`scripts/corrective-program/generate-corrective-program.ts`)

The only way to run the engine today (no coach UI yet). Reads a member's real findings (`--member <id>`) or accepts a synthetic `--patterns lower_cross:moderate,...` override for demos/testing without needing a seeded assessment; `--dry-run` prints without saving.

### Guard tests (3 new files, 55 tests)

`tests/corrective-engine-pattern-mapping.test.ts` (pure, 7 tests) — the finding→blueprint mapping rules, including the lumbar_posture/lower_crossed_pattern mutual-exclusivity rule. `tests/corrective-engine-session-builder.test.ts` (real local Supabase pool, no mocks, 39 tests across 6 pattern/severity combinations including the stacked Upper Cross + Forward Head case) — every hard rule from the task: no spinal-flexion exercise ever appears (checked against a real spinal-flexion id set loaded independently of the pool's own exclusion, so the exclusion is proven, not assumed), no stretch/mobility pick ever targets any active blueprint's long muscle, core is always the final block, every session stays within 8–12 exercises, stacked patterns produce zero duplicate exercises, severe has no strength block, same seed reproduces an identical program, a different seed produces different exercises. `tests/corrective-engine-save.test.ts` (real local Supabase, 1 test) — the full real pipeline (seed a real finding → detect → generate → save) plus the visibility/no-auto-assign guards.

**Deliberate break, done by hand this session**: temporarily reordered `buildSession` to push the Core block before Strength, reran the "always ends each session with the core block" test — 4 of 6 pattern/severity cases (every one with a nonzero strength budget) went red with `expected 'strength' to be 'core'`, the 2 severe cases (no strength block to reorder against) correctly stayed green — then reverted and confirmed all 47 tests green again.

### Verified

`npm run typecheck` clean (both workspaces). `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline (all new warnings are the expected `no-console` in the new CLI script, same convention as every other `scripts/*.ts` file). Full `npm test` (fresh `supabase db reset`, migrations through 131 applied cleanly) — 288/289 files, 3153/3154 tests passing, same pre-existing unrelated `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` flake (31 vs 30 — reconfirmed passing 6/6 alone on a fresh reset, zero changes to `lib/correlation-engine/` this session). `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` — compiled successfully. Re-ran `scripts/exercise-media/corrective-blueprint-gap-check.ts` after the blueprint-data refactor and diffed the regenerated report against git — byte-identical, confirming the refactor changed nothing about what it reports.

**Three full sample programs generated** (`--patterns` override, synthetic demonstration inputs — see this session's final report to the user for the complete week-by-week printout): (a) moderate Lower Cross, 3x/week; (b) severe Upper Cross + Forward Head stacked, 3x/week, no strength block confirmed; (c) mild Flat Back, 2x/week, full strength block confirmed.

## Corrective Programs coach screen — trigger, review/edit, approve & assign (2026-07-31)

The coach-facing UI for the Corrective Program Generator Engine (previous entry) — the engine had no way to run except a CLI script until now. Coach platform only; zero Your Move API video fetches; zero new member-facing code beyond the existing assigned-program surface.

### Screen flow (`app/coach/corrective-programs/`)

`/coach/corrective-programs` — member picker (reuses `listAssignedClients()`, same data source as the coach dashboard's client list). `/coach/corrective-programs/[memberId]` — shows the member's latest completed `static_posture` assessment findings with severity pills and the assessment date (reuses `getLatestCompletedPostureAssessment`/`detectCorrectivePatterns` from the engine), generation controls (2/3 days per week, equipment toggle chips defaulting to bodyweight/foam roller/small ball), and any `pending_coach_review` drafts already generated for this member. A member with no completed assessment (or one with findings that don't map to any of the 4 blueprints) gets a plain-language empty state instead of generation controls — never a "generate anyway" path. `/coach/corrective-programs/[memberId]/[groupTag]` — the draft review screen.

### Draft review screen (`DraftReviewPanel.tsx`)

Session-by-session cards, each session's blocks always rendered in MEF order (Release → Mobility → Stability → Strength → Core, Strength omitted entirely for severe drafts, matching the engine's own `SECTION_TYPE_BY_BLOCK` order — no client-side reordering logic, the DB's `sequence_index` order is trusted as-is). Every exercise row has Swap and Remove; every block has Add. Coach notes exist at both levels: per-session (`coach_notes`, editable per template) and per-program (reused `internal_notes` written identically to every session template in the group on save — no new column, since a "program" has no row of its own, just N templates sharing a `program_tags` group id). Regenerate re-runs the engine with a fresh seed against the same detected patterns and overwrites the existing templates' content in place (never creates a second draft group). Save Draft / Discard / Approve & Assign close out the screen.

### The qualified swap/add picker (`CorrectiveExercisePickerModal.tsx` + `lib/corrective-engine/blockQualification.ts`)

New `qualifiesForBlock(exercise, block, patterns)` — a faithful re-derivation of `sessionBuilder.ts`'s own per-block candidate filters (role match + tight/long muscle-slot match + the "never stretch a pattern's LONG muscle" cross-contamination rule), exposed as a standalone predicate so the picker can default to only offering exercises that would have been valid engine picks. Deliberately does **not** refactor `sessionBuilder.ts` itself to share this literally — that file has 39 passing guard tests and refactoring its generic `pickForSlots`/`pickStrengthBlock`/`pickCoreBlock` shape into a block-keyed predicate was judged not worth the regression risk for this task. Instead, `tests/corrective-programs-review.test.ts` proves the two agree empirically: every exercise a real generation run places in a block is asserted to satisfy `qualifiesForBlock` for that same block, across 3 pattern/severity scenarios including a stacked one — if the two ever drift, that test goes red. A "show full library" toggle switches the picker to the same catalog-wide search `/api/exercises` already powers in the general Program Builder; anything picked through that path is flagged as a coach override regardless of whether it happens to also qualify, since the coach explicitly stepped outside the guided default.

### New `is_coach_override` column (migration 132)

`coach_program_template_exercises.is_coach_override boolean not null default false`, additive only. `lib/coach-program-builder/templates.ts`'s `TemplateContentExerciseInput`/`replaceTemplateContent`/`duplicateTemplate` all pass it through — the existing content-save path (`saveProgramTemplateContentAction`, already used elsewhere in the Coach Program Builder) needed zero new server-action work to carry it.

### Approve & Assign (`lib/corrective-engine/review.ts`)

`approveCorrectiveDraftGroup` flips every session template in the group from `pending_coach_review` to `active` (`setTemplateStatus`, reused), then calls the existing `createAssignment` (`lib/coach-program-builder/assignments.ts`) once per session — 2 or 3 assignments, one per weekly slot, each on its own weekday (Mon/Thu for 2x, Mon/Wed/Fri for 3x) for 4 weeks, `publishImmediately: true`. **No new assignment/delivery code was written** — this is the exact same `createAssignment` path `assignProgramToClientAction` already uses for hand-built programs, so member delivery required zero new work. `regenerateCorrectiveDraftGroup` and `discardCorrectiveDraftGroup` (delete-all-templates-in-group) round out the lib; `listCorrectiveDraftGroupsForMember`/`getCorrectiveDraftGroup` group templates by the `corrective-program:<uuid>` tag `save.ts` already writes.

### Member delivery — already existed end to end, confirmed live

Investigated first per the task: `/programs` ("My Programs") and `/programs/[id]` (`MemberProgramsList`/`MemberAssignedWorkoutDetail`, `getMyAssignedWorkoutsAction`/`getMyAssignedWorkoutDetailAction`) already render any published `coach_assigned_workouts` row, coach-assigned or otherwise — nothing corrective-specific needed building here. Confirmed live with Playwright (below): after Approve & Assign, `member.one`'s own `/programs` page shows the new corrective program with no code changes on the member side.

### Real bug found and fixed via live Playwright testing (not just the test suite)

The swap picker's `excludeExternalIds` (meant to stop the picker offering an exercise already used elsewhere in the same block) included the exercise **currently being swapped** — so swapping the only qualified exercise for a thin slot (e.g. "Ball Release – Pecs," the sole release-role/pecs-targeting option under the default equipment) showed zero candidates, a dead end a coach would hit for real. Caught by driving the actual UI end-to-end (open picker → 0 results), not by the automated test suite, which never exercises the picker's exclude-list wiring. Fixed in `DraftReviewPanel.tsx`: the exclude list now omits the slot being swapped (`.filter((_, i) => i !== picker.exerciseIndex)`) while still excluding every other exercise already in that block. Re-verified live: the same swap now offers real alternatives and completes successfully.

### Guard tests (`tests/corrective-programs-review.test.ts`, 11 tests, real local Supabase)

Empty state (a member with no completed assessment yields `null`, not a generated program); a `pending_coach_review` draft has zero assignments and is unreadable by the member it's for (RLS, not just an app-layer check); Approve & Assign flips status to `active`, the assigned member's signed-in session can read the real published `coach_assigned_workouts` rows, and a *different* signed-in member gets zero rows back even filtering explicitly by the first member's id (proving RLS, not the query's own filter, is what's actually blocking cross-member reads); the qualification drift-check described above; hand-built fixtures pinning the exact negative rules (wrong role rejected even on a muscle match; the cross-contamination case; core requiring `core_stability` specifically; strength accepting any strength-role pick); the override flag stored `true`/`false` correctly for an override vs. an engine pick, and every engine-generated exercise defaults to `false`.

**Deliberate break, done by hand this session**: temporarily removed the Mobility block's "must not also stretch a LONG muscle" check from `qualifiesForBlock`, reran the cross-contamination test — went red (`expected true to be false`) — then restored it and reran to green.

### Verified

`npm run typecheck` clean (both workspaces). `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline, none in new files. Full `npm test` (fresh `supabase db reset`, migration 132 applied cleanly) — 289/290 files, 3170/3171 tests passing, same pre-existing unrelated `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` flake (31 vs 30). `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` — compiled successfully; new routes (`/coach/corrective-programs`, `/coach/corrective-programs/[memberId]`, `/coach/corrective-programs/[memberId]/[groupTag]`) all built.

**Verified locally with Playwright** (dev server + local Supabase, 390×844 mobile viewport, real `coach.one`/`member.one` seeded accounts, a real posture assessment with `rounded_shoulders` + `thoracic_kyphosis` findings seeded to produce a real Upper Cross detection): coach dashboard → Corrective Programs card → member picker → member findings screen (severity pills + assessment date, generation controls) → Generate Draft → draft review screen with blocks in the correct Release→Mobility→Stability→Core order and Session A labeled → opened the swap picker on a real exercise (confirmed the "show full library" toggle and the qualified-only default list) → swapped "Ball Release – Pecs (Chest)" for "Foam Roll – Lats" → Save Draft (no error) → Approve & Assign → redirected to the coach's client-programs page showing the now-assigned program → logged out, logged in as `member.one` → `/programs` shows the newly assigned corrective program. ## Protein Phase 1a — profile, safety screen, target calculation, coach approval (2026-07-31)

Foundation only, exactly per the task's scope: no food entry, no barcode, no ledger, no photo estimates, zero Your Move API calls. A member sets body weight + activity level, a safety screen gates automatic calculation, the target is calculated and either goes to a coach for approval (24-week program) or is shown as guidance (monthly/self-guided).

### Where it lives, and why

`/food-lens/protein` — a new sibling of `/food-lens/pattern` (Primal Pattern) and `/food-lens/preferences`, reached from a new card on the Food Lens hub (`app/food-lens/page.tsx`). Chose Food Lens over the generic `/profile` area because body weight and activity level are nutrition-calculation inputs, not general account settings, and this repo already treats Food Lens as the home for nutrition-specific member setup (Primal Pattern's protein/carb/fat emphasis lives there too, one card up).

### Safety screen: extends the existing nutrition safety table, doesn't duplicate it

Migration 133 adds `has_kidney_disease`, `has_significant_liver_disease`, `has_eating_disorder`, `has_medical_protein_limit` to migration 65's `member_nutrition_safety_flags` — the table already built for exactly this purpose (member-reported medical flags gating automatic nutrition guidance), already used by the Primal Pattern assessment. `is_pregnant` already existed there and is reused as-is. A dedicated `hasProteinSafetyOverride()` (`lib/health-safety/types.ts`) checks only the 5 fields relevant to protein safety — deliberately not the table's existing general `hasActiveOverride`, which also considers diabetes/insulin fields that have no bearing on protein safety. Submitting the protein form merges into whatever safety flags already exist rather than clobbering them, so the two features can never stomp on each other's data.

### Schema (migration 133)

Two new tables alongside the `member_nutrition_safety_flags` columns above:
- `member_protein_profile` — one row per member (weight in lb, activity-level key). Activity-level multipliers (1.0/1.2/1.4/1.6) are deliberately config-in-code (`lib/protein/calculation.ts`), not a DB column, same convention as correlation-engine weights and membership-tier ranks.
- `member_protein_targets` — append-only (one row per calculation request, never edited in place), so a later recompute never silently overwrites a coach's review of an earlier number. `track` ('structured_program' vs 'self_guided') is resolved server-side from the member's real `profiles.membership_tier` at submission time, never trusted from client input.

**The core guarantee — a 24-week program member never sees an active target before coach approval — is enforced at the database level, not just in the UI**: the member SELECT policy only ever returns a row where `status = 'active'`; a `pending_coach_review` row is genuinely unreadable by the member's own authenticated client, not merely hidden by app logic. The INSERT policy's `WITH CHECK` separately cross-references the member's real `membership_tier` via a subquery against `profiles` — a member cannot self-insert an already-`active` row by calling the API directly unless their real tier is actually a self-guided one, and even then only with `active_grams` equal to the computed number (no self-editing). Whether a member has a request outstanding is inferred at the app layer ("a profile exists, but no active row is visible") rather than via any column that would leak the pending number.

### Judgment calls (flagging for review)

- **24-week vs. monthly/self-guided mapping**: there is no dedicated "24-week program" flag anywhere in this schema. Mapped `membership_tiers.holistic_reset` (migration 69, this platform's structured coach-led tier) to the structured/24-week track, and `free_trial`/`membership` to self-guided (`lib/protein/track.ts`). Revisit if the business splits these differently.
- **Guidance range width**: ±10% of the computed number, rounded to the nearest 5g, with a 10g floor so small targets still get a meaningful spread (`getSuggestedProteinRange`, `lib/protein/calculation.ts`).
- **Safety-screen combined wording**: "an active or recovering eating disorder" is one yes/no item (matching the task's own phrasing), not two.

### Coach approval surface

`/coach/protein-review` — a queue list modeled directly on the existing `/coach/review-queue` (same card/status styling, open/resolved-style layout), only shown on the coach dashboard when something is actually pending (same convention as the Safety Review Queue card). `/coach/protein-review/[id]` shows the submitted weight/activity/computed number and a single input pre-filled with the computed value — approve as-is by leaving it, or edit it and save; either path is the same `approveProteinTargetAction`, which flips status to `active` and records `is_coach_edited` accordingly.

### Guard tests

`tests/protein-calculation.test.ts` (22 tests) — pure unit tests: rounding to the nearest 5g across many weight/multiplier combinations including an exact tie, the guidance-range math, `hasProteinSafetyOverride` (each of the 5 conditions blocks alone; diabetes-only flags do not), and the membership-tier-to-track mapping. `tests/protein-targets-review.test.ts` (7 tests) — real local Supabase (no mocks): a structured-program member's own client cannot insert an already-active row for itself even when it labels the row `track: 'self_guided'` to try to satisfy the policy; a pending row is genuinely unreadable by the member who owns it; the full flow (member submits → coach's queue shows it → coach approves as-is → member reads the real active target back); a coach edit stores a different `active_grams` than `computed_grams` flagged `is_coach_edited`; a different member can never read another member's row; a self-guided member's own client can insert and immediately read back an active row with no coach step, but cannot insert one with a self-edited `active_grams`.

**Deliberate break, done by hand this session**: temporarily replaced the INSERT policy's `membership_tier` cross-check with `and true`, reset the local DB, reran the suite — the "member cannot self-insert an already-active row while their real tier is holistic_reset" test went red (`expected null not to be null`, i.e. the bypass insert that should have been rejected went through) — then restored the real check, reset again, and confirmed all tests green.

### A real bug found and fixed via live testing, not just the automated suite

The member-facing form's "blocked" (safety-screen) view had no way back to the form — `pending_review` and `active` states both offered an "Update your info" link, but `blocked` didn't, so a member who'd misclicked a safety checkbox (or whose situation later changed) had no UI path to revisit it. Caught while driving the real flow with Playwright, not by the test suite (which doesn't exercise this UI path). Fixed in `ProteinProfileForm.tsx` by adding the same "Update your info" link to the blocked state.

### Verified

`npm run typecheck` clean (both workspaces) — fixed two build-time issues along the way: Next's typed-routes plugin needed `as Route` casts on the four new `/coach/protein-review*` links (new routes, not yet in `.next/types` from a prior build), and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` needed the coach-approval action to omit `error` entirely on success rather than set it to `undefined`. `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline, none in new files. Full `npm test` (fresh `supabase db reset`, migration 133 applied cleanly) — 292/292 test files run, 1 failing test (`correlation-engine-integration.test.ts`, the same pre-existing unrelated 31-vs-30 flake documented in every recent entry in this doc), all 29 new protein tests passing. `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` — compiled successfully; new routes (`/food-lens/protein`, `/coach/protein-review`, `/coach/protein-review/[id]`) all built. Next's `'use server'` file restriction (only async function exports allowed) meant the safety-block message string had to live in `lib/protein/copy.ts` rather than `app/actions/protein.ts` — a real compile error caught by the build, not just assumed.

**Verified locally with Playwright** (dev server + local Supabase, 390×844 mobile viewport, real `member.one`/`coach.one` seeded accounts, real server actions and RLS — no mocking): checked the eating-disorder safety box → submitted → saw the exact caring block message, confirmed it persists across a page reload (not just in-memory state). Cleared the flag, submitted as a self-guided member (default seeded tier) → saw the guidance range (165 lb, regular movement → 90g, range shown, labeled "guidance, not a prescription"). Flipped the same member to the `holistic_reset` tier and resubmitted (200 lb, muscle-building emphasis) → saw the "your coach is setting up your target" message with no number anywhere in the page. Logged in as the coach → dashboard showed the Protein Targets card → queue showed the real submission (200 lb, computed 145g) → opened it, entered an edited value (150g), saved → queue emptied. Logged back in as the member → saw the real active target (150g, "Set by your coach"), proving the coach's edit — not the computed 145g — is what the member sees. All ad-hoc verification scripts were scratch files outside the repo/deleted before commit; no test data left in local Supabase afterward.

**Migrations to push** — one migration is pending against production: 133 (the 4 new safety-flag columns plus `member_protein_profile`/`member_protein_targets`, additive only, no existing behavior changes). Combined with the migrations noted as still-possibly-unpushed in the prior three entries (127 through 132), one command applies whichever of them the production DB doesn't have yet — `supabase db push` tracks by version number, so anything already applied is skipped automatically:

## Protein Phase 1b — barcode scanning scouting (2026-07-31)

Investigation only, exactly per the task's scope: no product features, no member-visible changes, no migration. Answers "does camera barcode scanning actually work in iPhone Safari, and what should the real ledger build on" before any ledger gets built.

### What already existed — a full barcode-scanning pipeline, already shipped

Checked first, per "reuse existing systems": this codebase already has a complete, production barcode-to-nutrition pipeline in Food Lens, distinct from Food Lens's photo-analysis path. `components/food-products/BarcodeScanner.tsx` opens the camera and decodes live — the native `BarcodeDetector` Web API where available (Chrome/Android), falling back to `@zxing/browser` everywhere else (notably Safari, which has never shipped `BarcodeDetector`) — plus a manual-digit-entry mode, a "camera denied" recovery screen, torch toggle, and camera-switch. `components/food-products/BarcodeScanFlow.tsx` wires that into a full wizard (scan → `lookupBarcodeAction` → cache-or-fetch from Open Food Facts directly via `lib/food-products/providers/openFoodFacts.ts` → `analyzeProductScanAction` → results page), already live at `/food-lens/barcode/new`. `lib/food-products/barcode.ts` validates UPC-A/UPC-E/EAN-8/EAN-13 with real GS1 checksums. This already captures protein grams per serving (`product_nutrients.protein_g`) — it just isn't wired to a protein ledger yet, because there is no ledger yet.

This is a materially more capable scanner than anything scouted below: it costs no external-vendor quota (talks to Open Food Facts directly, free/no-key), and it already handles the Safari case (zxing fallback) that native `BarcodeDetector` cannot. **The real ledger should reuse `BarcodeScanner.tsx` and `lookupBarcodeAction` as-is** rather than build a new scanning integration — this session's test page (below) reuses the exact same `BarcodeScanner` component for that reason, changing only which backend the decoded barcode gets sent to.

### Does live camera scanning actually work in iPhone Safari?

Not investigated from memory — read the actual code path Safari would hit. `BarcodeScanner.tsx`'s own `hasNativeBarcodeDetector()` check means: iOS/iPadOS Safari has never implemented the `BarcodeDetector` Web API (it remains a Chromium-only feature, no WebKit ship date as of this session), so every iPhone Safari user falls through to the `@zxing/browser` path automatically — already coded, already the fallback for exactly this case. `getUserMedia` with `facingMode: 'environment'` and the `<video playsInline muted>` attributes (already present) are the two things iOS Safari requires for in-page (non-fullscreen) live camera video — both already satisfied. HTTPS is required for `getUserMedia` on any origin except `localhost`; `app.mefwellness.com` already serves HTTPS, so this is a non-issue in production (would only block a plain-HTTP local IP test, not relevant here). Camera permission in Safari is a one-time per-origin prompt, persisted after the first grant — same UX members already get from Food Lens's meal-photo capture, which uses the same `getUserMedia` pattern.

**Verdict: yes, live scanning works in iPhone Safari, via `@zxing/browser`, and this isn't a guess — it's already shipping.** `BarcodeScanFlow.tsx` has been live at `/food-lens/barcode/new` since the barcode feature was built, so the zxing fallback this session is recommending is not new/untested code — it has real production traffic already. This session's own test page (below) additionally confirmed the same `BarcodeScanner` component initializes its camera and renders correctly in a real browser session (Playwright, fake camera device — see Verified section for what a real device would still need confirming).

### Library choice

`@zxing/browser` (wrapping `@zxing/library`) is what's already installed and wired — no alternative was evaluated for this task since reuse beats rebuild and this one already meets the bar: works in Safari, small (the barcode feature's `/food-lens/barcode/new` route builds at 4.55 kB route-specific JS, zxing loaded via dynamic `import()` only when the native detector is absent, so Chrome/Android users never pay for it), restricted to the 4 formats this product needs (`UPC_A`, `UPC_E`, `EAN_8`, `EAN_13` via `DecodeHintType.POSSIBLE_FORMATS`), and already has real usage. Low-light performance wasn't separately benchmarked (no real device available in this environment — see below) — mitigated in the existing UI by a torch-toggle button shown whenever the camera track reports torch capability.

Coach-only (redirects non-coaches, and `middleware.ts`'s existing blanket `/coach/*` coach-role gate covers it too), not linked from any navigation — reachable only by typing the URL. `npm run typecheck` clean (both workspaces). `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline, none in new files. ## Protein Ledger (Phase 1b) + app-wide white-label sweep (2026-07-31)

Prerequisite check passed: Phase 1a (profile/safety screen/target calculation/coach approval, migration 133) is live — verified `member_protein_profile`/`member_protein_targets` and `getMyProteinSetupState`'s four states all work exactly as documented above. The barcode-scouting verdict was treated as positive per the task (the scouting session above could not test a real iPhone camera — see its own "Honest limitation" note — but the user confirmed real-device scanning separately), so the ledger ships with scanning included.

### The big decision: no new ledger schema at all

Before building anything, checked for an existing system per this repo's standing rule — and found one. Migration 59's `member_food_log` + `food_products` + `product_nutrients` (already live, already used by Food Lens's barcode/search/manual-entry flows, edit/delete already built in `FoodLogList.tsx`) is exactly "a member's confirmed-grams food entries." Building a parallel `protein_entries` table would have duplicated working, tested, RLS-correct code for no reason. The Protein Ledger is a protein-focused *read* over that same table, plus one new lightweight write path (quick add) that reuses the same private-product pattern Food Lens's manual entry already established (`insertVerifiedFoodProductFromLabelScan`, `data_source = 'mef_verified'`, barcode null — never shared/deduped). Consequence worth knowing: because this is the same table, any food a member logs anywhere else in Food Lens via barcode/search/manual entry (not just via the new Ledger screen) also counts toward their protein tally automatically — one unified log, not two competing ones. Meal-photo entries (AI-estimated macros, `product_id` null) are explicitly excluded from every ledger query — confirmed-grams only, per the task.

New files: `lib/protein/ledger.ts` (pure grams/rounding/day-grouping/target-display logic, unit-tested), `app/actions/protein-ledger.ts` (today/history reads + log/quick-add/resolve-search-result actions — reuses `startFoodLensScanAction`, `lookupBarcodeAction`, `searchFoodsAction`, `insertFoodLogEntry`, `editFoodLogEntryAction`, `removeFoodLogEntryAction`, `insertVerifiedFoodProductFromLabelScan` as-is; deliberately skips `analyzeProductScanAction`'s rules-engine/Root-coaching pipeline since the ledger only needs a protein number, not a full nutrition-quality review), `components/protein-ledger/*` (progress card, entry lanes, entries list, 7-day history), `app/food-lens/protein/ledger/page.tsx`.

`/food-lens/protein/ledger`, linked from a new card on the Food Lens hub showing a live "Xg of Yg today" (or "Xg logged today" pre-target) subtitle. Progress card branches on the same four `getMyProteinSetupState` stages Phase 1a's own summary card uses, via one new pure function (`resolveLedgerTargetDisplay`, unit-tested for exactly the task's two hard rules): active shows a real bar against `active_grams`; pending-review and blocked both show the tally with **no** target number and **no** setup link; blocked additionally gets no nudge at all (not even "not started" styling); not-started is the only state with a "set up your target" link. Entries list shows time + a lane label (Scanned/Searched/Quick add, inferred from what's already on the row — no new column) + grams, with edit (adjust servings, live-recalculates grams) and delete, both reusing the food log's existing actions verbatim.

**Day rollover**: member's device timezone, via `profiles.timezone` (already captured elsewhere in the app) and `lib/time/localDate.ts`'s `todaysLocalDate`/`localDateStringFor` — the same helper already used by check-ins, weekly reports, and coaching insights, so "today" means the same thing everywhere in the app. Writing this test exposed a real, pre-existing bug in that shared helper: its timezone conversion silently depended on the *host process's own* local timezone, not just the target timezone (it worked correctly only when the server process itself ran in UTC — true on Vercel, not true when running tests locally in a non-UTC timezone, which is exactly what caught it). Fixed via `Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts` instead of a `toLocaleString`-then-reparse round trip — same function signatures, zero behavior change for any caller already running under TZ=UTC, now also correct everywhere else. Left `app/actions/checkin.ts`'s separate `resolveLocalDate` untouched (different implementation, tightly coupled to check-in's late-submission grace window, out of scope here).

This actually caught two real bugs before they shipped, both fixed and re-verified:
1. **Total didn't refresh after editing/deleting an entry.** `ProteinLedgerEntries.tsx` updated its own list optimistically but never told the sibling progress card (a separate server-fed component) to recompute — so the "Xg of Yg" header could go stale the moment a member edited or deleted something. ## Protein Ledger: search race fix, generic-food ranking, numeral legibility (2026-07-31)

Targeted bug-fix pass on the Ledger's search lane and the Today's Protein card — no schema change, no rebuild of the ledger itself, per the task's own scope.

### 1. Search results vanishing (the reported bug)

Root cause confirmed exactly as the task suspected: `SearchLane`'s debounce (`components/protein-ledger/ProteinEntryLanes.tsx`) only throttled when a request was *dispatched* — it never guarded against one arriving out of order. A natural typing pause (e.g. after "chicken", before "breast") could let an earlier, shorter-query request stay in flight while a newer, longer-query request was also dispatched; whichever happened to resolve *last* won, so a correct, populated result set could be silently overwritten by a stale, often-empty response for an already-superseded partial query — exactly "briefly shows results, then reverts to Nothing found."

Fixed with a new pure guard, `shouldApplySearchResponse` (`lib/protein/ledger.ts`) — a response is only applied if its request id is still the latest one dispatched *and* its query still matches what's live in the box right now (checked via a ref, not the async closure's stale copy of `query`, which would otherwise always trivially match itself). `isSearching` now stays true from the moment the query changes until an *accepted* response lands, and "Nothing found" never renders while it's true — a "Searching…" state shows instead. True network-level cancellation (aborting the in-flight request) isn't available here since `searchFoodsAction` is a Next.js Server Action, not a raw `fetch` under this code's control — discard-on-resolve via the id/query check is the standard, correct substitute and matches "cancel in-flight requests" in effect: a stale response's network call still completes, but its result can never reach the screen.

Verified live (not just unit-tested): typed "chicken breast" one character at a time with real per-keystroke delays against a seeded cached product, polled the rendered text every 200ms for 2 seconds after typing stopped — "Nothing found" never appeared at any point, and the results, once shown, never disappeared again.

### 2. Generic foods ranked first

Investigated what's actually available to rank on. Open Food Facts' `cgi/search.pl` (what `OpenFoodFactsProvider.searchByName()` already uses) returns name/brand/image only — no popularity, category, or generic/branded flag. (A newer official Search-a-licious API does expose brand/category/popularity fields, but swapping the provider's HTTP endpoint is a bigger, separate change than this task's scope and wasn't made here — flagging it as a real option for a future session if richer ranking signals are wanted.) The app's own product cache (`food_products`) has no such flag either. Conclusion stated directly per the task's own fallback: **neither source can distinguish generic from branded**, so this ranks by closeness of the product name to what was actually typed instead — the task's own suggested fallback.

New `rankFoodSearchResults` (`lib/food-products/search.ts`): exact case-insensitive name match ranks first, then a name that starts with the query, then one that merely contains it, then everything else; ties within a tier broken by shorter name (a plain "Chicken Breast" outranks "Tyson Chargrilled Chicken Breast Tenders, Frozen"). Applied to both `searchCachedFoodProducts`'s and `searchFoodsAction`'s external-provider results — both now over-fetch a small candidate pool before ranking and slicing to the final shown count, so there's actually something to reorder among. This is shared by the original `/food-lens/search` page too (same `searchFoodsAction`), a positive side effect, not scope creep — it's the exact same shared function the Ledger's search lane already depended on.

Verified live: seeded a generic "Chicken Breast" (no brand) and a branded "Tyson Chargrilled Chicken Breast Tenders, Frozen" into the local cache (the sandbox's external OFF search was unreliable this session — see below — so this proved the ranking against real, working data instead), searched "chicken breast" in the Ledger, and the generic entry rendered first, branded second.

### 3. "0g" reading as "og"

Confirmed visually (screenshot, not assumed) — Cormorant Garamond's old-style figures render its zero nearly identical to a lowercase o at the Today's Protein card's display size. Fixed with `font-variant-numeric: lining-nums` on both of `ProteinLedgerProgress.tsx`'s number displays, verified by screenshotting before and after: the same serif display font, but the zero now has the flat top/bottom of a lining figure, unambiguous at a glance. Chose this over swapping to the body font (DM Sans) because it worked and keeps the design language fully intact — no font-family change needed anywhere in the card.

### Guard tests

`tests/protein-ledger-logic.test.ts` — 3 new `shouldApplySearchResponse` tests, including the literal out-of-order scenario the task asked for (a request for "c" dispatched first, resolving *after* a request for "chicken breast" that was dispatched second, is correctly discarded even though it completed successfully). `tests/food-products-search-ranking.test.ts` (new file, 5 tests) — exact match beats a longer branded name, starts-with beats contains, shorter name breaks ties, empty query leaves order untouched, a null product name never crashes or drops a result.

### Verified

`npm run typecheck` clean. `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline. Full `npm test` (fresh `supabase db reset` — same reason as last entry: driving the app locally to verify this pollutes two unrelated tests' fixtures every time, confirmed and cleaned the same way) — 294/295 test files, 3234/3235 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` flake (31 vs 30). `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` — compiled successfully; `/food-lens/protein/ledger` now 6.02 kB route-specific JS (was 5.8 kB).

**Verified locally with Playwright**, real member.one session, real server actions — see each fix's own "Verified live" note above for what was actually driven and screenshotted.

**Honest limitation, still true this session**: Open Food Facts' legacy search endpoint returned an HTML "temporarily unavailable" page rather than JSON again this session (both the legacy `cgi/search.pl` scraping endpoint currently used and the equally-legacy `/api/v2/search` REST endpoint failed the same way; the newer Search-a-licious API at `search.openfoodfacts.org/search` worked fine and returned real, well-structured JSON when tested directly). Since the user's own bug report describes seeing real branded results, this is most likely transient/sandbox-network-specific rather than a universal outage — the provider's endpoint was deliberately left unchanged this session (out of scope for a targeted fix), but if external search continues to come back empty in production, switching `OpenFoodFactsProvider.searchByName()` to the Search-a-licious endpoint is the recommended fix, and would also unlock real brand/category/popularity data for even better ranking than the exact-match heuristic used here.

**No migration to push** — no schema changed in this pass either.

The old "Protein ledger" and "Protein target" cards are gone, replaced by one card reusing the existing `ProteinLedgerProgress` component (built in the Protein Ledger Phase 1b task) — it already encodes exactly the three states the task asked for (no target → setup nudge, pending coach review → clear pending message and no progress bar, target set → "Xg of Yg" with a fill bar), including the lining-numerals fix so "0g" never reads as "og." This let me *drop* a data fetch rather than add one: `getMyProteinSetupState()` was being called a second time just for the old separate "Protein target" card, and `getProteinLedgerTodayAction()` already calls it internally, so the page now fetches protein state exactly once. The card is wrapped in a link to the ledger whenever a target exists in any form (active/pending/blocked); when no target exists yet, the component's own internal "Set up your protein target" link is the only interactive element (avoids a nested `<a>`).

### 4. Primal Pattern: permanent card → dismissible banner

New `components/food-lens/PrimalPatternSetupBanner.tsx` (client component). Only rendered at all when the member has no active Primal Pattern profile (server-checked); closing its X hides it for the rest of the browser session via `sessionStorage` (not `localStorage` — deliberately not permanent), reappearing on a fresh session if still unset. Once a pattern is set, the banner — and the destination link that used to live in it — disappears entirely, per the task's explicit "must not occupy space for members who've completed it." This is a real reduction in reachability for that one destination once a pattern exists (no compact fallback link was added elsewhere on the page) — a deliberate reading of that instruction over the task's general "every destination stays reachable" framing; worth confirming this was the intended tradeoff.

New `tests/food-lens-page-redesign.test.ts` (25 tests: subheading swap, Log food section structure, merged-card states via `resolveLedgerTargetDisplay`, banner session-scoping, unchanged section order) — all passing, plus the pre-existing `food-lens-navigation`/`subhead-contrast-ratio`/`protein-ledger-logic` suites re-run clean against the new file. ## Food Lens: protein ledger reachability + scan verdict consistency (2026-07-31)

Two bugs reported from a real production scan, both fixed. No schema change, no design-system or layout change beyond what each fix required.

### 1. Protein ledger unreachable for a member with no target yet

Root cause confirmed exactly as suspected: the redesign's merged protein card (`app/food-lens/page.tsx`) only wrapped itself in a `<Link href="/food-lens/protein/ledger">` when `proteinTargetState.stage !== 'not_started'` — a deliberate choice at the time (documented in the entry above) to avoid nesting an `<a>` inside another `<a>`, since `ProteinLedgerProgress`'s own internal "Set up your protein target" link only renders in that exact state. The side effect: a brand-new member — `not_started` is the default state for every member until they finish setup — had **zero** link to the ledger anywhere on `/food-lens`. The ledger page itself (`app/food-lens/protein/ledger/page.tsx`) never gated on target stage — it always rendered `ProteinEntryLanes` (barcode/search/quick-add) and the running total regardless — so this was purely a lost entry point, not a torn-down feature.

Confirmed via full code trace (not assumed) that four of the five "Log food" tiles on the redesigned page (Scan a Barcode, Scan a Label, Search, Manual Entry) already write confirmed grams into `member_food_log` with a non-null `product_id` — the exact same store the ledger's total sums over — so a member using those tiles was still contributing to their protein total the whole time, just with no way to see or manage that total without a target already set up. Only "Scan a Meal" (the AI photo estimate) is deliberately excluded from the ledger, by design (`lib/protein/ledger.ts`: "confirmed grams only, never estimated").

**Fix chosen: restored the ledger's own always-reachable entry point**, rather than rewiring the five tiles (they were already correctly wired). `app/food-lens/page.tsx`'s merged card now always wraps in the `<Link>` to `/food-lens/protein/ledger`, in every target stage. To keep the nested-anchor fix from before intact, `ProteinLedgerProgress` (`components/protein-ledger/ProteinLedgerProgress.tsx`) gained a `setupLinkIsInteractive` prop (default `true`); the food-lens page passes `false` so its own internal "Set up your protein target" text renders as plain text there (the whole card is already one tappable link to the ledger, which has its own real, working setup link once you land on it). This matches how the ledger was originally built — always reachable, target-optional — rather than inventing new behavior.

Verified the protein target setup flow itself is intact and unaffected: `/food-lens/protein` renders `ProteinProfileForm`, submits via `submitMyProteinProfile`, and shows the resulting summary card in place — reachable and working. It doesn't auto-redirect anywhere after completion (pre-existing behavior, not touched).

### 2. Meal scan verdict sections contradicting each other

All three sections (red/yellow/green banner, Macro Balance, Root's Take) are computed once per scan from the same vision-model call's output (`app/actions/food-lens.ts`), but each is a separate classification function reading that shared data — nothing forced them to agree in wording.

**(a) Banner contradicted Macro Balance/Root's Take on fat.** `computeMealQualityRating`'s red "sugar-driven" branch (`lib/food-lens/mealQuality.ts`) built its explanation from two hardcoded template strings that unconditionally claimed "little meaningful protein, fat, fiber, or nutrient density" — regardless of what the SAME macro estimate feeding Macro Balance actually said about fat. Fixed: the explanation is now built dynamically, only naming a macro as absent when both the quality signals AND that scan's real macro levels agree it's low or none. A latte with real cream/sauce fat (moderate, per Macro Balance) no longer gets told it has "little meaningful fat" in the banner above it.

**(b) Banner described a generic category instead of the actual item.** The same branch picked between exactly two hardcoded phrasings — "a regular sugary soda" or "a sugary snack" — based only on a beverage/food boolean, never the item's real name. A matcha latte got called a soda. Fixed: the vision model's own detected-item label (the first non-condiment item, e.g. "Iced Matcha Latte" over its own "Vanilla Sweet Cream"/"Pistachio Sauce" condiments — new `primaryMealSubjectLabel` helper) is now the subject of the sentence, e.g. "Iced Matcha Latte with Vanilla Sweet Cream and Pistachio Sauce reads as a sweetened beverage, with carbohydrates coming primarily from added sugar and low nutrient density and little meaningful protein or fiber."

**(c) "Compared against your My Eating Pattern pattern."** `pattern_label` defaults to the literal string "My Eating Pattern" (`PrimalPatternForm`'s pre-filled default, which most members never change) — which already ends in the word "pattern," so the caption's naive `${patternLabel} pattern` template doubled it. Same bug existed a second time in `coachingNarrative.ts`'s deterministic fallback sentence ("your ${patternLabel} pattern") — caught only because the live verification below drives the actual no-LLM-configured path this dev environment runs. Both now go through one shared `possessivePatternPhrase`/`formatPatternComparisonCaption` (`lib/food-lens/comparison.ts`) that only appends "pattern" when the label doesn't already end with it.

**(d) Root's Take claimed a confident match with no real data behind it.** Checked what actually backs a "Match" claim: `primal_pattern_profiles` is a one-time, self-entered record (`PrimalPatternForm`'s own docblock: "no Primal Pattern questionnaire scoring engine exists in this codebase yet") — there is no historical/statistical eating baseline anywhere in this codebase that a scan is compared against. The instant a member saves any profile, even by accepting every default (protein/carb/fat emphasis all `moderate`, label untouched), a full Match/Heavier/Lighter verdict renders with no distinction from a genuinely configured target. New `isPatternBaselineThin` (`lib/food-lens/comparison.ts`) treats "label still the untouched default AND all three emphases still moderate" as the only signal this schema can offer for "this member hasn't told us anything real yet" — the closest honest proxy available, since the target isn't statistically derived and can't be measured for confidence any other way. When thin: `generateFoodLensCoachingNarrative` (`lib/food-lens/coachingNarrative.ts`) short-circuits before ever calling the LLM or building a match claim, returning a fixed "you haven't set up the real details of your eating pattern yet" line instead; `PatternComparisonCard` skips the Match/Heavier/Lighter chips and swaps the caption for a setup nudge. Nothing is deleted from storage — `comparison.signals` still persist normally for the registry/correlation-engine consumers that read them — only the member-facing claim of a confident match is suppressed until the pattern is genuinely customized.

### Guard tests

`tests/food-lens-meal-quality.test.ts` — updated the existing Sprite/snack regression tests to assert the actual item name renders (not a hardcoded "soda"/"snack" guess), added a `primaryMealSubjectLabel` describe block (3 tests), and a direct regression test reproducing the real production scenario numbers (sweetened latte, real moderate fat, high carb, low protein) proving the explanation never claims "little meaningful fat" while naming the real item. `tests/food-lens-comparison.test.ts` — `isPatternBaselineThin` (4 tests: thin default, renamed label survives thinness check as not-thin, one changed emphasis survives as not-thin, fully customized), `formatPatternComparisonCaption`/`possessivePatternPhrase` (regression tests for the exact doubled-word bug plus the normal append case). New `tests/food-lens-coaching-narrative.test.ts` — `buildDeterministicFallbackNarrative` directly, including the same doubled-word regression, since this is the path this dev environment's own unconfigured LLM provider actually exercises. `tests/food-lens-page-redesign.test.ts` — replaced the two tests that asserted the old `proteinCardIsTappable` gate existed with tests asserting the opposite: the card is always wrapped in exactly one `Link`, in every stage.

### Verified

`npm run typecheck` clean. `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline. Full `npm test` (fresh `supabase db reset` first) — 296/297 test files, 3277/3278 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` flake documented in every recent entry in this doc, unrelated to this work. `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` — compiled successfully.

**Verified locally with Playwright** (dev server + local Supabase, real `member.one@example.test` session, real server actions/RLS, 390×844 mobile viewport, no mocking) — logged in, loaded `/food-lens` with the seed account's default `not_started` protein state, confirmed exactly one real `<a href="/food-lens/protein/ledger">` exists on the page, clicked it, and landed on the ledger page with its Scan/Search/Quick add lanes rendered (`Protein ledgerToday's protein0gSet up your protein targetScanSearchQuick add...`) — the actual reported bug, reproduced and confirmed fixed. Seeded two real scans via service-role insert (mirroring the exact reported production scenario — an "Iced Matcha Latte with Vanilla Sweet Cream and Pistachio Sauce" with high added sugar, low nutrient density, real moderate fat) against a thin (untouched-default) and then a genuinely customized Primal Pattern profile, computing the persisted `signals`/`narrative`/`rating`/`explanation` by calling the actual fixed production functions (not hand-typed fixtures), and loaded both scan detail pages live: the thin-baseline scan rendered the item-named banner with no "soda," no fat contradiction, no doubled "pattern," no Match/Heavier/Lighter chips, and the "haven't set up the real details" message in place of a claimed match; the customized-pattern scan rendered the same consistent banner plus real chips and a correctly-worded "Compared against your My Low-Carb Pattern" caption. This run also caught a real bug before it shipped: the deterministic fallback narrative (the path this dev environment's own unconfigured `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` actually exercises) had the same doubled-"pattern" bug as the caption, missed by the first pass since it only touched the caption string — fixed by routing both through the same helper, then re-verified live. All seeded rows deleted afterward and a final `supabase db reset` run before the last full-suite pass.

## Core Values Snapshot — Experience 1 of the free-tier lineup, built end to end (2026-07-31)

New member-facing assessment, the app's new free entry point. Built entirely on the existing Unified Adaptive Assessment Runtime (`lib/assessment-runtime/`, `lib/assessment-foundation/`) and published through `lib/assessment-registry/registry.ts` — no new session/scoring engine, per the task's hard constraint. WBSA (the one other real consumer of that runtime) was used as the reference pattern throughout; every deviation from it is a small, deliberate, documented addition, not a parallel system.

### What shipped

**The seven-beat flow** (`components/core-values-snapshot/CoreValuesSnapshotTaker.tsx` + supporting components) — Intro → 3 question screens (Q1-4 single-select one at a time, Q5-10 six sliders on one screen, Q11 single-select, Q12 dynamic two-option forced choice) → What Root Learned (one of four branches) → Gap Visual + Key Insight (+ conditional S1 observation) → Weekly Experiment offer → Resource (summary-first, expandable full piece) → Closing reinforcement + Progress card + Handoff, all in one continuous client-side flow over the same `persistAnswer`/`completeSession` runtime calls WBSA uses. Every member-facing string is the brief's own final copy, used word for word (`lib/core-values-snapshot/copy.ts`).

**Navigation is Continue-only, no auto-advance** — a deliberate divergence from `WbsaTaker.tsx`'s 350ms auto-advance timer, made because of the documented `project_checkin_navigation_stability_fix` lesson (auto-advance caused real stability bugs in the check-in wizard). Each screen has an explicit Back/Continue pair instead.

**Scoring, branching, and randomization** (`lib/core-values-snapshot/{scoring,q12,randomize,experiment}.ts`) — pure, no I/O, unit-tested. Importance (Q1/Q2/Q3 +1, Q4 +2, Q11 +2, Q12 winner +1, range 0-8), attention (raw 1-5 from the sliders), top/runner-up with the Q4→Q12→Q11→canonical-order tiebreak chain, gap classification (≤2/3/≥4 → clear_gap/slipping/aligned), the split flag (Q11 pick scored 0 across Q1-4, computed as its own subtotal before Q11/Q12 points are added), and S1 (guilt-area attention ≥4, suppressed entirely on the split branch). Q1-4/Q11 option order and the six sliders' order are shuffled with a seeded, deterministic PRNG keyed off `sessionId` — stable within a session/across resumes, varies per member. Q12's two options are generated live from the member's own Q1-4 answers (never stored as fixed content); the three-way-tie rule (pit the Q4 answer against the next-highest other area) is implemented and tested.

**Content is 100% migration-seeded**, matching WBSA's own pattern exactly — `supabase/migrations/00000000000134_core_values_snapshot.sql`: a catalog row (`assessment_definitions`/`assessment_definition_versions`), one `unified_assessment_definitions` row, 3 sections, 12 questions. No question sets `concern_category`/`severity_tags`/`validation.findingRule` — this is a values/preference instrument, not a symptom instrument, so it deliberately produces **zero** Universal Registry findings (a documented scope decision, not an oversight; same posture as Primal Pattern's classification-only design).

**Registry**: `core-values-snapshot` added to `AssessmentKey` (`lib/assessment-registry/types.ts`) and to `ASSESSMENT_REGISTRY` (`registry.ts`) — `minLevel: 'free_trial'`, `allowedLevels` all three tiers, confirmed this is exactly what "FREE tier, visible to everyone" means in this codebase (`catalog.ts`'s own `isPremium = minLevel !== 'free_trial'`). Also had to add a `core-values-snapshot` entry to `lib/investigation-engine/registry.ts`'s `INVESTIGATION_METADATA` (a `Record<AssessmentKey, ...>` the compiler enforces exhaustively) and to `lib/root-coaching-engine/questions.ts`'s conversation-type question pool — both real, load-bearing systems that key off every `AssessmentKey`/`ConversationType`, not cosmetic.

### The Weekly Experiment (Beat 5) — real reuse, minimal real additions

The 7-day, 5-minutes-a-day experiment reuses `lifestyle_experiments` (migration 92) as-is for the experiment record itself (title = the protected value's display label, protocol = the theory/experiment text, `recommendation_id` left null since this isn't Recommendation-Engine-sourced like every other row in that table today) — same lifecycle, same `MAX_ACTIVE_EXPERIMENTS` cap, same read-time `expired_no_reflection` derivation, zero new experiment engine.

Two small, necessary additions on top, both migration 134:
- `lifestyle_experiments.source_session_id` — one new nullable column so a completion traces forward to the exact experiment it started (needed for accurate per-completion coach visibility and retakes). `startLifestyleExperiment` gained an optional `sourceSessionId` param; every other existing caller is unaffected.
- `cvs_experiment_daily_logs` — one new table for the daily Yes/Not-today tap and the day-3 qualitative response (same date row; day-3's response is a one-time thing tied to a specific calendar date, not worth a third table). RLS mirrors every other member/coach-scoped table in this codebase.

**Day-3/day-7 follow-ups reuse the existing "From Root" delivery pipeline** (Root Coaching Conversation Engine, `member_coaching_messages`, the dashboard's `CoachingMessageCard`) rather than building a new notification system, per the brief's explicit instruction. Concretely: two new `ConversationType` values (`cvs_day3_checkin`/`cvs_day7_result`, additive migration constraint extension, same drop/re-add pattern migration 99 already used); a new optional `precomposedMessage` field on `CoachingCandidate` so these two types skip the generic template/rotation pipeline entirely and use their own final, verbatim copy (`service.ts`'s `planCoachingConversation` checks for it before falling back to `composeCoachingMessage`); a new pure candidate builder (`lib/core-values-snapshot/coachingCandidates.ts`) mirroring `selector.ts`'s own `experimentCandidates` shape; and a new optional `cvsCandidates` field threaded through `SelectorInput`/`PlanCoachingConversationInput` (backward compatible — every existing caller that omits it is unaffected). `app/actions/rootCoaching.ts`'s `gatherAndPlan` now splits fetched `lifestyle_experiments` into CVS-sourced (`recommendation_id is null`) and Recommendation-Engine-sourced, so the *generic* `experimentCandidates()` doesn't also generate its own midpoint/overdue messages for the same CVS experiment CVS's own day-3/day-7 candidates already cover — `buildMemberEngagementProfile` still sees the full unfiltered list, so consistency scoring is unaffected. `CoachingMessageCard.tsx` routes to a real destination (`/assessments/core-values-snapshot/experiment`) instead of the read-only bottom sheet when the day's message is one of these two types, since the day-3 response needs a real place to be tapped in, matching `NoticingTile`'s own documented `href`-vs-`sheet` split.

The daily tap, day-3 check-in, and day-7 reflection all live on `components/core-values-snapshot/CvsExperimentPanel.tsx`, shared by the in-flow taker (right after "I'm in"), the standalone results page (on revisit), and the dedicated `/assessments/core-values-snapshot/experiment` page (reached from the dashboard nudge). Day-7's reflected pattern (mostly-yes vs. patchy) is computed from real stored `cvs_experiment_daily_logs` rows, never invented — `classifyDay7Pattern`, unit-tested.

### "What Root Knows So Far"

No existing "Root observation with category/message/open-thread" API exists in this codebase (confirmed by grep — `narrative_items`, `member_coaching_messages`, and `health_timeline_events` are the three closest systems, none an exact match). Used `narrative_items` (Member Health Narrative, migration 29) as the real, existing "member's Root knowledge record" — closest fit, has a `member_visible` flag and a dedup-by-(category,title) discipline already. On completion, `app/actions/coreValuesSnapshot.ts` writes up to four entries (top/runner-up, gap status, open thread "what's pressing on {top}", and the S1 guilt-observation entry only when S1 fired) via `insertNarrativeItem`/`findActiveItem`/`supersedeNarrativeItem` directly (not through `lib/narrative/service.ts`, which is wired to the AI-agent dispatch pipeline and doesn't fit this call site). Rendered inline at the end of the in-flow taker (fetched client-side once the Close beat is reached, since the items don't exist yet at page-load time) and via a reusable `WhatRootKnowsCard` server component on the standalone results page.

### Coach visibility

`CoreValuesSnapshotPanel` (list, counts-only) + `/coach/clients/[id]/core-values-snapshot/[sessionId]` (full detail) — same split WBSA's own coach surfaces use, wired into `app/coach/clients/[id]/page.tsx` alongside `WbsaPanel`. The detail page shows everything the brief asked for: full importance ranking (all six areas with scores), attention map, top/runner-up/gap classification + split flag, which branch ran + whether S1 fired, the verbatim Q3 guilt answer, Weekly Experiment status (accepted/skipped, daily yes/no streak, day-3 response, outcome reflection if closed), completion date + time-to-complete, and a "continued to Experience 2" field — honestly hardcoded to always read "not yet, Experience 2 doesn't exist yet" rather than fabricating a real-looking answer, since the Life Signal Check hasn't shipped. No new RLS grant needed — rides the same `coach_read_assigned_unified_assessment_sessions`/`_answers` (migration 99) and new `coach_read_assigned_cvs_experiment_daily_logs` (migration 134) policies.

### What's honestly not built

The Life Signal Check and Readiness Pulse (Experiences 2 and 3) don't exist — the Progress card and Handoff screen render them as locked/upcoming and the "Start the Life Signal Check" button is a real disabled/coming-soon state, never a dead link, per the brief's own instruction.

### Guard tests

`tests/core-values-snapshot-scoring.test.ts` (19 tests, pure) — all four Beat 3 branches including the split-takes-priority-over-slipping rule, the Q4→Q12→Q11 top-value tiebreak on a real tie, runner-up excludes top, S1 fires only above the attention threshold and never on split even with high guilt-attention, Q12's two-highest-areas generation plus the three-way-tie Q4-vs-next-highest rule plus never-identical-options, seeded-shuffle determinism/variation/no-drop-or-duplicate, day-3/day-7 eligibility date math, mostly-yes vs. patchy pattern classification from real logged rows, and the narrative-draft builder (S1 entry appears only when S1 fired). Also updated three pre-existing test fixtures (`lifestyle-experiments-lifecycle`, `root-coaching-engine-engagement`, `root-coaching-engine-selector`) to include the new `sourceSessionId` field, and two hardcoded-count assertions (`assessment-registry-integration`, `investigation-engine`) that needed bumping from 9 to 10 assessments — normal maintenance from adding a real 10th registry entry, not new behavior.

### Verified

`npm run typecheck` clean. `npm run lint` (repo root) — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline, no new files flagged. Full `npm test` after a fresh `supabase db reset` (migration 134 applied cleanly) — 297/298 test files, 3304/3305 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` date-math flake documented in every recent entry in this doc, re-confirmed deterministic and unrelated (re-ran that file alone, same failure, no CVS code anywhere near it). `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` — compiled successfully; all four new member routes generated (`/assessments/core-values-snapshot`, `/take` 5.23 kB, `/results/[sessionId]` 3.45 kB, `/experiment` 2.15 kB) plus the coach detail route (866 B).

Separately confirmed the dedicated `/assessments/core-values-snapshot/experiment` page is reachable on its own and correctly shows "Day 1 of 7" from the same real stored experiment. Then logged in as the coach, opened the client page, confirmed the `CoreValuesSnapshotPanel` renders the real completed session with a "Top: / Runner-up:" summary line, followed the real detail link, and confirmed the full detail page — attention map, branch shown, verbatim Q3 answer, Weekly Experiment section with a real daily streak line, and the Continued-to-Experience-2 field — all rendered from the actual member data, not placeholders. A `supabase db reset` was run before and after this session (before to apply migration 134 cleanly, after to restore a pristine seed state), matching this repo's own documented practice for local Playwright runs against the shared dev Supabase instance.
